Reproducible PRIO-GRID workflows

Source: vignettes/reproducible-workflows.Rmd
reproducible-workflows.Rmd

priogridR keeps data conversion, quality assessment, combination, and export in one explicit workflow. This vignette uses small offline data so that every step can run during package checks.

Construct two cell-period datasets

The first source has one observed missing value and several structurally absent cell-periods. These are different conditions and should not be treated as interchangeable.

climate <- data.frame(
  pgid = c(1, 2, 1, 2),
  year = c(2020, 2020, 2021, 2021),
  temperature = c(21, NA, 22, 20)
)

population <- data.frame(
  pgid = c(1, 2, 1, 2),
  year = c(2020, 2020, 2021, 2021),
  population = c(100, 80, 103, 82)
)

Inspect metadata and structure

pg_metadata() reports only information that is stored in or supplied with an object. It does not invent source provenance for an ordinary data frame.

pg_metadata(climate, config = config, time = "year")
#> <pg_metadata>
#>   Object: data.frame
#>   Grid: 2 x 3 (6 cells)
#>   Variables: temperature
#>   Time: year (2 periods)
pg_describe(climate, time = "year", config = config)
#> <pg_description>
#>   Rows: 4; cells: 2; periods: 2
#>   Variables: 1; duplicate keys: 0
#>   Balanced over observed domain: yes

Separate coverage from missingness

Coverage uses the six configured cells and two requested years as its explicit reference. Missingness, by contrast, uses only rows that actually exist.

pg_coverage(
  climate,
  time = "year",
  variables = "temperature",
  config = config,
  reference_time = 2020:2021
)
#>   n_expected n_present n_structurally_absent n_outside_reference
#> 1         12         4                     8                   0
#>   n_observed_missing coverage_share
#> 1                  1      0.3333333

pg_missingness(climate, variables = "temperature", time = "year")
#>      variable n_observed n_missing n_non_missing missing_share
#> 1 temperature          4         1             3          0.25

An absent row does not imply a measured zero. Use pg_complete_panel() only when a complete panel is substantively required, and provide fill values only for variables with meaningful structural zeros.

Check compatibility and combine sources

pg_assert_compatible() checks grid, CRS, temporal, and key definitions. pg_bind() applies these safeguards before joining variables.

pg_assert_compatible(
  climate,
  population,
  config = config,
  time = "year"
)

analysis_data <- pg_bind(
  climate,
  population,
  along = "variables",
  config = config,
  time = "year"
)
analysis_data
#>   pgid year temperature population
#> 1    1 2020          21        100
#> 2    2 2020          NA         80
#> 3    1 2021          22        103
#> 4    2 2021          20         82

Row-wise binding is also supported. Duplicate keys and conflicting values fail by default; conflict = "first" or "last" must be requested explicitly.

Compare versions

pg_compare() distinguishes keys found in only one dataset, paired missing values, one-sided missing values, and unequal observed values.

revised <- climate
revised$temperature[revised$pgid == 1 & revised$year == 2021] <- 22.25

comparison <- pg_compare(
  climate,
  revised,
  time = "year",
  variables = "temperature",
  config_x = config,
  config_y = config
)
comparison
#> <pg_comparison>
#>   Compatible: yes
#>   Keys: 4 shared; 0 x-only; 0 y-only
#>   Variables compared: 1
comparison$variables
#>      variable class_x class_y n_shared_keys n_equal n_unequal n_paired_missing
#> 1 temperature numeric numeric             4       2         1                1
#>   n_one_sided_missing mean_difference max_abs_difference
#> 1                   0     -0.08333333               0.25

Apply existing utilities and export

The checked result remains an ordinary data frame and can be passed directly to temporal, spatial, plotting, and output functions.

analysis_data <- pg_temporal_lag(
  analysis_data,
  variable = "temperature",
  time = "year"
)

pg_write_result(analysis_data, "analysis-data.parquet")

For a reproducible analysis, record the input data release, grid configuration, variable semantics, transformations, and package version alongside the result. pg_metadata() provides a common schema for this information, but it cannot recover provenance that was never recorded.
